title: Seed study: seed, prompt, and model contributions to generated image variance (specificity ladder, 240 images)
description:
Artifacts and analysis for a study measuring how much of a generated image is determined by the random seed alone, relative to the prompt and the model.

Design: a specificity ladder of 6 nested rungs (3 to 35 words) across 2 prompt families (landscape, object), crossed with 2 SDXL-class models (stable-diffusion-xl-1024-v1-0, playground-v2-1024px-aesthetic), 10 seeds per cell. 240 images, fully balanced across 24 cells, generated via the Fireworks API with all generation parameters held constant within a cell.

Contents: all 240 full-resolution PNGs; the manifest binding each artifact to its (prompt, model, seed); VLM captions; cached feature matrices for two views (56 perceptual statistics, and 768-d embeddings of the captions); the full variance decomposition; and paper figures plus a browsable gallery.

Analyses included: (1) an orthogonal variance decomposition into prompt, model, prompt x model, and seed, with EMS-corrected variance components; (2) a specificity floor curve measuring how much run-to-run randomness added prompt constraints actually remove; (3) a seed-signature test asking whether a seed value carries a consistent effect across unrelated prompts; (4) an intent-legibility classifier measuring whether the prompt can be recovered from the artifact.

Key findings: the prompt dominates semantic variance (62.4% vs 30.9% for the seed), but the seed carries a statistically significant cross-prompt signature (p = 0.001) concentrated in spatial luminance features, and roughly 31% of the semantic randomness at a three-word prompt survives a thirty-five word one.
notes: Images were generated by Stable Diffusion XL 1.0 and Playground v2, whose own model licenses (CreativeML OpenRAIL-M and the Playground v2 Community License respectively) govern use of the generated images. The CC-BY-4.0 license declared here applies to the analysis, metadata, captions, feature matrices, and figures authored by the depositors.
